section_title: Why does Paul thank Prisca and Aquila?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 3 Greet Prisca and Aquila, my fellow workers in Christ Jesus, 4 who have risked their lives for me. Not only I but all the churches of the Gentiles are grateful to them. 5 Greet also the church that meets at their house. Greet my beloved Epenetus, who was the first convert to Christ in the province of Asia.

context_lines: Paul greets Prisca and Aquila as fellow workers in Christ who risked their lives for him. His gratitude is shared by the Gentile churches. Their service has mattered beyond a private friendship.

He also greets the church meeting at their house and Epenetus, the first convert to Christ in Asia. The word church is ekklēsia (ek-klay-SEE-ah), ἐκκλησία, an assembly or community; see [Thayer’s entry](https://biblehub.com/greek/1577.htm). Here Paul distinguishes the gathered people from the house where they meet.

Prisca is also called Priscilla in Acts. [Acts 18:24–26](https://biblehub.com/bsb/acts/18.htm) describes the couple helping Apollos understand God’s way more accurately. Their household and their work provide support for both people and the message they share.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly read these greetings as honoring a couple’s costly partnership and a community gathering in their home. Paul gives thanks for service that includes risk, hospitality and work alongside others. The church at their house is a body of people to be greeted, not simply an address.
god_plan_lines: [1 Corinthians 16:19](https://biblehub.com/bsb/1_corinthians/16.htm) also sends greetings from Aquila, Prisca and the church at their house. Their hospitality belongs to a wider pattern of homes supporting the life and work of believers.

[Ephesians 2:19–22](https://biblehub.com/bsb/ephesians/2.htm) develops the larger picture of believers as God’s household and a dwelling place for Him by the Spirit, with Christ as the cornerstone. A house provides a meeting place; God is forming the people who gather into a shared life in Him.
current_position_lines: Worship as the Early Church Knew It understands the church here as the community of believers, distinct from the building in which they meet. The house provides a place for the assembly; the people are the church. The study uses this passage to emphasize shared spiritual life and service rather than identifying the church with an address.
